import sqlite3

def handle(event, db):
    # Ignore events that are not checkout completion or async payment success
    if event["type"] not in (
        "checkout.session.completed",
        "checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded",
    ):
        return "ignored"

    checkout = event["data"]["object"]
    # Only fulfill when payment_status is 'paid'
    if checkout["payment_status"] != "paid":
        return "pending"

    # Use the full checkout session id as the processed event identifier
    event_id = checkout["id"]
    session_id = checkout["id"]
    amount = checkout["amount_total"]
    currency = checkout["currency"]

    # Begin a transaction that will be atomic with respect to concurrent invocations
    with db:
        # Attempt to insert into processed_events; if it already exists, we have already fulfilled
        cur = db.execute(
            "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO processed_events(event_id) VALUES (?)",
            (event_id,),
        )
        if cur.rowcount == 0:
            # This session has already been processed – idempotent return
            return "already_fulfilled"

        # At this point we know this is the first time we see this event_id.
        # Insert the shipment with the exact amount and currency from the event.
        db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO shipments(session_id, amount, currency) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (session_id, amount, currency),
        )

    return "fulfilled"

limitation: Synthetic, already-authenticated checkout fixtures under the documented Python/SQLite contract. Verifies persisted shipment records for these cases; not proof of production correctness or physical exactly-once shipping. Real signature verification, external fulfillment and production outbox delivery are outside this lab. Repair holdouts are unseen only on the first model attempt. Final audit inputs are generated after the patch freezes and never returned to the model; a failed audit withholds verification. The in-VM driver is not an adversarially tamper-proof grader.
